'''Bloodwood trees''' are a special type of [[tree]] native to [[Vampyrium]]. Chopping them requires completion of [[The Blood Moon Rises]], 77 [[Woodcutting]] and an empty [[bucket]], yielding [[bloodwood sap]] which can be used to upgrade [[arrow]]s into [[seeking arrows]]. These arrows are very powerful, as they possess a +20 accuracy and minimum of 3 damage when a [[successful hit]] lands compared to normal arrows. An [[aranei bucket dealer]] standing near the two bloodwood tree locations will supply buckets free of charge via their "Take" or "Take-many" [[option]]s.

Unlike traditional woodcutting, chopping bloodwood trees is far more click-intensive; efficiently chopping bloodwood trees involves clicking multiple times a tick to wound a tree, and managing the bleeding of multiple trees at once. When cut efficiently using a 2-tick cycle, approximately 90-100 buckets of bloodwood sap can be obtained per hour.

Alternatively, the [[engorged bloodwood tree]] can also be chopped as a lower-intensity alternative more similar to traditional woodcutting, although at considerably reduced rates of sap, offering only ~20 buckets per hour.

When using the [[Bucket of bloodwood sap|bloodwood sap]] to make [[sap-treated redwood logs]], an hour's worth of bloodwood sap can make up to 10,500 [[seeking arrow shaft]]s. These can then be [[Fletching|fletched]] into powerful [[seeking arrows]]. Using this method, an hour's worth of chopping can yield enough sap to profit {{Coins|{{GEP|Seeking amethyst arrow|10500}} - {{GEP|Amethyst arrow|10500}}- {{GEP|Redwood logs|100}}}} for [[seeking amethyst arrow]]s and {{Coins|{{GEP|Seeking dragon arrow|10500}} - {{GEP|Dragon arrow|10500}} - {{GEP|Redwood logs|100}}}} for [[seeking dragon arrow]]s. However, keep in mind that processing the [[sap-treated logs]] and fletching the [[seeking arrows]] takes time, which reduces hourly profit rates.

==Mechanics==
===Wounding a tree===
[[File:Cutting bloodwood tree.mp4|thumb|autoplay|loop|Efficiently cutting a bloodwood tree]]
Bloodwood trees are chopped individually between players, meaning that a group of players can chop the same tree without interfering with each other. This however doesn't improve the woodcutting rate as it usually does with other trees.

To start, players must click on the tree with an empty [[bucket]] in the inventory. This places the bucket on the tree, which cannot be retrieved until it is filled with [[Bucket of bloodwood sap|bloodwood sap]]. Players then need to click on their character to pull back their axe.

Every chop requires the player to pull the axe back twice, however both clicks can be performed on the same tick. Once the axe is fully pulled back, click the tree to chop it. Efficiently cutting a bloodwood tree is a two tick cycle: Clicking the tree, clicking the player character twice, then repeating.

An efficient chopping cycle will result in a smooth animation of the player character swinging their axe as if they were cutting a regular tree. The amount of chops required is dependent on the player's [[Woodcutting]] level and the [[axe]] used.

Bloodwood trees do not drop any nests nor leaves, and do not trigger any [[Forestry]] events. Additionally, the [[lumberjack outfit]] and its variants ''do not'' increase experience gained. [[Forester's ration]]s are consumed with a felling axe at the engorged tree to reduce chopping time by roughly 10 seconds, but have no effect and are not consumed at the active bloodwood trees. However, visible Woodcutting boosts '''do''' improve the chopping rates.

===Draining wounded trees===
[[File:Draining bloodwood tree.gif|thumb|width=220x220|A wounded bloodwood tree filling a bucket with sap.]]
Once a bloodwood tree has been fully wounded, sap will start draining into the bucket; while this occurs, the tree's health bar will steadily deplete, allowing players to work on wounding another tree if they so desire.

To maximize chopping rates when chopping all three trees, tap the two bleeding trees only when both have fully depleted their health bars. This will allow players to always have a new tree to chop once the current tree has finished being wounded. A bleeding tree's health bar will drain in roughly half the time it takes to wound a tree, making the half-way point of the current tree a good indicator for when to tap the other trees.

Every time players tap a tree, they will gain some Woodcutting experience, for a total of 1,364 per tree. Once the bucket is full, click on the tree to pick it up, then replace it with another bucket. Swapping buckets occurs automatically if players were already focused on that tree from a previous tap.

Players may scale their experience rates by chopping one, two, or all three trees at the same time. Chopping all 3 trees at the same time can net upwards of 245k Woodcutting experience per hour. If chopping all 3 trees at the same time, the location south of the [[Ruined Village]] is slightly better, since all 3 trees there are exactly 4 tiles away from each other.

Note that teleporting away from the trees resets any progress on them, including partial drainage.
